connections.why: Choosing a legal entity is a first decision for any business
Objectives must balance competing stakeholder interests
External growth often turns firms into multinationals
Marketing objectives flow from overall business objectives
Growth must be funded from appropriate finance sources
Structure shapes how leadership and delegation operate
Leadership style strongly affects employee motivation
Good communication supports motivation and engagement
Organizational structure determines communication flows
Break-even analysis is built directly on costs and revenue
Costs and revenues feed into the final accounts
Ratios are calculated from the final accounts
Finance choices affect a firm's cash flow position
Investment decisions depend on available finance
Marketing planning operationalises the marketing role
Research informs segmentation and positioning decisions
Positioning guides decisions across the marketing mix
Pricing in the mix depends on the firm's cost structure
Operations method influences the best location choice
The chosen operations method shapes the cost structure
Break-even informs whether an investment will be viable
Employees are a key stakeholder managed through HRM
Product decisions must be deliverable by operations
